   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, JANUARY 24, 2023
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:36 p.m.
on Tuesday, January 24, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Brenhaug.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Jacqueline Borja, Michelle Brenhaug, Viki Goto Jorge Herrera,
  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez and Riaz (Rick) Khan

Commissioners Absent:  Susan Fitzsimmons

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

The Commission had a moment of silence to remember the victims, families and communities
affected by the recent gun violence, particularly those lost in Monterey Park on January 21.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by Commissioner
  Khan to table agenda item 4D until the next meeting.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JANUARY 24, 2023
   Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0-1 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Brenhaug, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Borja

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

  3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Borja and seconded by Commissioner
  Herrera to approve the updated minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular
  Meeting for January 24, 2023.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0-1 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Brenhaug, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Fitzsimmons

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING COMMISSIONERS
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez announced that two commissioners will not be returning
  for another term.

  The Commission thanked Commissioner Fitzsimmons and Commissioner Borja
  for all their work in the HEAR Commission.

  B. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the update on this item.

  The Commission requested that the results from the Youth Engagement Survey
  and information regarding the Land Acknowledgment Statement be posted and/or
  linked to the HEAR Commission web page. They would like to consolidate the event
  pages and add photos. The Commission also requested guidelines for website
  content.

  Public Comment: None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JANUARY 24, 2023
   C. 2023 MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO PLANNING
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the update.

  The Commission asked if October 1st would conflict with Dumplings & Beer in
  regards to staffing. They commented that October would be better for students
  since they start school in September. The Commission discussed signage, the
  budget, length of event, souvenirs, and sponsorships. Instead of having a
  subcommittee to plan the event, they decided to set time aside during each
  meeting until October so that everyone can contribute.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Herrera offers support and prayers to community. He commends
  gentleman from Alhambra for his bravery.

  Vice-Chair Goto offers her condolences to victims. She provided information for
  the Los Angeles Department of Mental Health Hotline and the GoFundMe for
  Monterey Park victims. She recently attended the City of Hope Community Benefit
  Advisory Committee meeting. She offered information regarding the 2023 Healthy
  Living Grant. Vice-Chair Goto wanted to acknowledge that February is African-
  American Heritage Month and recommended a PBS American Experience program,
  Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space. She also shared that she applied for
  StoryCorps: One Small Step.

  Commissioner Borja shares everyone’s sentiments regarding the Monterey Park
  tragedy.

  Commissioner Brenhaug voiced her feelings regarding the Monterey Park tragedy,
  the importance of mental health and community care.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez encouraged the community to utilize the resources. Also,
  she is volunteering for Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority’s homeless count
  in San Gabriel. She hopes the local library will have a book exhibit for Black History
  month. Chair Jennings-Nuñez will be sponsoring an art exhibit at Blossom Market
  which will be displayed there for the next two months.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens announced that two new commissioners will begin at the next
  meeting. There will be a commission re-organization. He also mentioned that the

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 7:40 p.m.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  January 24, 2023

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2023 Draft Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the draft Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
Commission and is intended for the 2023 calendar year.

Purpose of the Commission
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.

Scope of the Commission
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission and outline
the areas of focus for the remainder of 2023. It includes proposed programs and projects
that will be implemented and completed throughout the year, some of which may extend
beyond 2023. Some of the items have carried over from the 2022 workplan.

DRAFT 2023 WORKPLAN
The 2023 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission has
identified as key areas of interest in furtherance of its purpose. The following list of ideas,
